summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, gastroparesis, and cardiac conditions was admitted with fever, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. Initial evaluation revealed leukocytosis and imaging showed diffuse colonic wall thickening consistent with colitis and mild pulmonary edema. Blood cultures grew methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA), leading to a diagnosis of MSSA sepsis, likely originating from the dialysis graft. The patient was treated with intravenous antibiotics, which were narrowed to cefazolin after culture results. He developed minor serosanguinous oozing from the graft site, attributed to repeated needle access, but no infection was found. His symptoms improved with treatment and dialysis. He remained afebrile, with resolving leukocytosis, and was discharged on a six-week course of cefazolin administered post-dialysis, with follow-up planned with infectious disease and outpatient colonoscopy for colitis evaluation.
